userStories.title: GBC 2bpp tile parser
userStories.description: Implement a parser that decodes GBC 2bpp tile data. Each tile is 16 bytes encoding an 8x8 pixel grid. For each row (2 bytes), bit N of byte 0 is the low bit and bit N of byte 1 is the high bit of the color index (0-3) for pixel N. The parser should decode a single tile (16 bytes → Uint8Array of 64 color indices) and parse a full buffer into an array of tiles.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/gbc/GbcTileParser.ts exists with decodeTile(data: Uint8Array, offset: number) → Uint8Array(64)
decodeTile correctly maps 2bpp encoding: for each row, byte0 bit N = low bit, byte1 bit N = high bit of pixel (7-N) color index
parseTileBuffer(buffer: ArrayBuffer) → Uint8Array[] returns array of 558 tiles for an 8928-byte buffer
Unit tests in tests/assets/gbc/GbcTileParser.test.ts verify known bit patterns: all-zero bytes → 64 zeros, 0xFF 0x00 → all 1s, 0x00 0xFF → all 2s, 0xFF 0xFF → all 3s
Edge case: buffer size not divisible by 16 throws descriptive error
npm run test passes

userStories.title: Color palette system
userStories.description: Implement a color palette system that maps 2-bit color indices (0-3) to RGBA values. Index 0 is always transparent. Provide a default green palette matching GBC style, plus red and blue presets. Include a renderTileToCanvas() function that takes a decoded tile (Uint8Array of 64 indices) and a palette, and renders it to an 8x8 HTMLCanvasElement.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/gbc/GbcPalette.ts exports GbcPalette type as [RGBA, RGBA, RGBA, RGBA] where RGBA is [r,g,b,a]
DEFAULT_PALETTE: index 0 = transparent (alpha 0), indices 1-3 = green shades matching GBC aesthetic
RED_PALETTE and BLUE_PALETTE presets exported
renderTileToCanvas(tile: Uint8Array, palette: GbcPalette) → HTMLCanvasElement (8x8 canvas)
Index 0 pixels are fully transparent (alpha = 0)
Unit tests in tests/assets/gbc/GbcPalette.test.ts verify palette mapping and transparency
npm run test passes

userStories.title: Sprite frame composer
userStories.description: Implement a composer that assembles 4 tiles in a 2x2 grid into a 16x16 character sprite canvas. Also create a data table mapping animation frame names to tile indices within the 558-tile set. At minimum, define walk animations for 4 directions x 2 frames.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/gbc/SpriteFrameComposer.ts exports composeFrame(tiles: Uint8Array[], tileIndices: [number, number, number, number], palette: GbcPalette) → HTMLCanvasElement (16x16)
Tiles are arranged: [topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft, bottomRight] in the 2x2 grid
src/assets/gbc/SpriteTileMapping.ts exports SPRITE_FRAME_MAP: Record<string, [number, number, number, number]>
Frame map includes at least: walk_down_1, walk_down_2, walk_up_1, walk_up_2, walk_left_1, walk_left_2, walk_right_1, walk_right_2
Unit tests in tests/assets/gbc/SpriteFrameComposer.test.ts verify 16x16 output dimensions and correct tile placement
npm run test passes

userStories.title: Async sprite sheet loader
userStories.description: Implement an async loader that fetches .bin files, parses tiles, composes frames, and returns a Map of named HTMLCanvasElement sprites. Load all 9 characters in parallel. Keys follow the pattern oracle_{characterName}_{frameName} (e.g. oracle_ganondorf_walk_down_1). Handle fetch errors gracefully (log warning, skip character).
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/gbc/GbcSpriteLoader.ts exports loadOracleSprites() → Promise<Map<string, HTMLCanvasElement>>
Fetches all 9 .bin files from /sprites/oracles/ in parallel using Promise.allSettled
For each character, composes all frames defined in SPRITE_FRAME_MAP
Map keys follow pattern: oracle_{charName}_{frameName} e.g. oracle_ganondorf_walk_down_1
If a fetch fails, logs a console.warn and continues loading other characters
Returns a Map with (9 characters × number of frames) entries on success
Unit tests in tests/assets/gbc/GbcSpriteLoader.test.ts mock fetch and verify map key format and canvas dimensions
npm run test passes
